Trend Watch: Which classics should you buy in 2025?

Featured carsGuides
American Hagerty Inc., a major lifestyle and membership community within the car world, as well as the world's largest provider of specialty insurance for classic vehicles, is known to many vehicle enthusiasts. Now they have released a list of classic cars to keep an extra eye on during the coming year - and several of these feature frequently on our website.
Tomas JönssonJanuary 07, 2025 10:00

Hagerty Automotive Intelligence analyzed data from public and private sales, together with historical trends and insurance valuations, to narrow the list down to 11 car models. We highlight three of these, as these three have appeared a little more frequently on Bidders Highway.

It's worth noting that the price of the car alone was not the only factor considered, but also valuations such as driving enjoyment and what enthusiasts think, when this list was published. You'll find the full list at the bottom of the page, but these three caught our interest a little extra.

Datsun 280ZX

The Datsun 280ZX became a bit slower and heavier than the earlier Z-cars, and ended up being more of a grand tourer and less of a pure sports car. Datsun was convinced that customers would rather prioritize comfort, space and more luxurious equipment. As a result, most enthusiasts passed over the model, but have come to realize the fact that the ZX captures much of the original Z's appeal at a fraction of the cost - especially when equipped with a turbo under the hood. Prices have increased by 138% since 2019, but the analysis suggests there's still room for appreciation.

Volvo P1800

What it lacks in speed, it makes up for in style - the Volvo P1800's Italian curves make it look far more expensive than it is. Today's "Next Gen collectors" appreciate that equation and consistently pay more for these cars than older enthusiasts do, which is a good indication that this Swedish coupé will continue to be appreciated around the world. Extra fun to see a Swedish model on the list, of course.

Jaguar E-Type

The Jaguar E-Type Coupe was first shown at the Geneva Motor Show in 1961, and its beautiful lines still move enthusiasts to their very soul while its engine makes the heart race. The valuation of this British classic has retreated considerably over the past three years, but that has brought it within reach of a new generation of enthusiasts. "Gen X" interest has grown by 8% in just the past year, which could cause prices to recover, and in time perhaps even start climbing again.
